# Tools

Tools are framework-free `ToolSpec` values (`berg_agents/core/tool_spec.py`): name, description, JSON-Schema params inferred from the function signature, and an `execute` callable. They serialize to OpenAI function-calling or Anthropic tool-use shape, validate args through generated Pydantic models, and carry a risk class (`low` / `medium` / `high`).

## Built-in tools

`berg_agents/agents/factory.py:create_tools()` wires the file tools bound to a workspace root:

| Tool | Risk | Purpose |
|------|------|---------|
| `read_file` | low | Read file contents (workspace-relative or `/workspace/`-prefixed) |
| `edit_file` | high | Replace a file's contents |
| `write_file` | high | Create or overwrite a file |

The workspace root mounts at `/workspace/`; path normalization blocks escapes (`..`, `~`, absolute paths outside the root).

## Capabilities

`berg_agents/capabilities/tool_adapter.py:tool_to_capability()` wraps a `ToolSpec` as a `Capability` (kebab-case id, intent from description, input model from params) so tools dispatch through the standard audited envelope flow. Risk is inferred — sensitive MCP servers and explicit `risk_class` win, read-only name hints (`read`, `search`, `lookup`, `list`, `get`, …) map to low, everything else is medium.

Custom subagents implement `AbstractAgent` and register via `app.register_agent(name, agent)`.

## MCP tools

External MCP servers (stdio subprocess or HTTP) contribute tools prefixed `mcp_<server>__<tool>`, so names never collide. Sensitive servers (`github`, `memory`) pause for approval; read-only servers (`context7`, `docs`, `reference`) run without interruption. See [Configuration](CONFIGURATION.qmd) for the `mcp.json` format.

## Human-in-the-Loop

Mutating tools pause the run by default (`write_file`, `edit_file`, `delete`, `execute`). The caller resumes with approve (tool runs, cycle continues), reject (an error is fed back to the model, tool never runs), or edit (args rewritten before dispatch). TUI approves inline; the web HITL surface offers Approve / Reject / Edit with raw interrupt data for debugging.
